Walmart's agent profiles go live

Walmart's Agent Gateway is reported live with Meta's Muse as its first agent, with spending-limited Agent Profiles. Also: Gemini 4 Neon's price sheet, Google's sovereign AI accelerator for European startups, and a new gateway from Psionic AI. Plus a follow-up on Anthropic's shares and the deadlines ahead.

Stories

Story of the day · Retail and agents Reported

The Verge reported on November twenty-third that Walmart's Agent Gateway is live, with Meta's Muse as the first supported agent, according to Unite AI. Muse can find and buy Walmart products, including Black Friday deals, through customer-controlled Agent Profiles. The first time an item goes in the cart, the shopper sets up a profile with a spending limit and approval rules. Purchases are kept in a separate history. Prices match Walmart.com, and Walmart's return policy applies. Crypto Briefing says the gateway relies on the Model Context Protocol. Walmart reportedly said more agents are on the way. The framework was first announced on October twenty-first. Separately, commercetools said menswear retailer DXL is exposing its catalogue to Muse, with real-time pricing and availability.

The readWhat this really signals: the pending launch from last week has become a working pattern. An agent gets its own identity, a separate purchase history and a hard spending cap, and it enters through a dedicated door, not the storefront. For a retailer, that is a reference design to compare with your own. Specify how an agent authenticates, which limits apply, how an order is logged and how it is reversed. Note the pairing: Walmart builds the gateway itself, while DXL relies on a commerce vendor to feed the same agent. Both need clean, real-time product data and prices. Worth watching: how many agents Walmart admits, and on what terms.

Models and vendors Confirmed

Google announced Gemini 4 Neon on November eighteenth, and updated its blog post on November twenty-third. It costs three dollars per million input tokens, fifteen cents per million cached input tokens, and fifteen dollars per million output tokens, with a one million token context window. It is rolling out in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, in Gemini for business, and for paid Pro and Ultra subscribers in Antigravity and the Gemini app.

The readThe bigger picture: the cached price is ninety-five percent below the standard input price, so your real bill depends on cache hit rate. The post names the Gemini API and business surfaces. Check regions and quotas before adding a route, and rerun your own evaluation set first.

Sovereignty and Europe Reported

Google Cloud has launched an accelerator called Sovereign AI for Europe and Israel, according to SecurityBrief. It is a twelve-week, equity-free programme for late-seed to Series A companies with regulated AI workloads. It offers engineering mentoring, advice linked to AI Act regulatory sandboxes, and guidance on sovereign deployment options. It follows Google's Brussels announcement bringing Gemini to partner-operated Google Cloud Dedicated.

The readReading between the lines: hyperscalers are now seeding the European sovereign ecosystem as a customer funnel. That makes startups in it candidates for your vendor scans, but check who operates the infrastructure and who holds the keys before treating any of them as a sovereign alternative.

Platform Reported

Psionic AI has officially launched OpenGateway, according to DigitalToday. The gateway serves open-weight models optimised with the company's own kernel from its edge data centres, behind an API key. It offers team-level permissions, spending limits and per-request logs. An on-premise version is offered for closed networks in finance and the public sector.

The readWhy it matters: team quotas, spend caps and request logs are becoming the baseline of any gateway product. The speed claims come from the vendor, so test throughput and quality yourself. And ask whether you can keep your own gateway in front of a hosted one.

Follow-up

Expected: whether Anthropic's market slide would continue. Result: on Monday, November twenty-third, the shares slipped to about eighty-eight dollars, roughly five percent above the eighty-three dollar IPO price, while other AI stocks rallied, according to Bloomberg and AOL.

Number of the day

Ninety-five percent. That is the discount on cached input tokens for Gemini 4 Neon: fifteen cents per million, against three dollars per million at the standard input price. Cache hit rate now shapes your cost model.
